text:
Predicates:
Employee(x) ::: x is an employee.
ScheduleMeeting(x, y) ::: x schedules a meeting with y.
Customer(y) ::: y is a customer.
AppearToday(x) ::: x appears in the company today.
LunchInCompany(x) ::: x has lunch in the company.
LunchAtHome(x) ::: x has lunch at home.
RemoteFromHome(x) ::: x is working remotely from home.
InOtherCountry(x) ::: x is in another country.
Manager(x) ::: x is a manager.
James ::: James (constant).
Premises:
∀x (ScheduleMeeting(x, y) ∧ Customer(y) → AppearToday(x)) ::: All employees who schedule a meeting with their customers appear in the company today.
∀x (LunchInCompany(x) → ScheduleMeeting(x, y)) ::: Everyone who has lunch in the company schedules meetings with their customers.
∀x (LunchInCompany(x) ∨ LunchAtHome(x)) ::: Employees either have lunch in the company or at home.
∀x (LunchAtHome(x) → RemoteFromHome(x)) ::: If an employee has lunch at home, then he/she is working remotely from home.
∀x (InOtherCountry(x) → RemoteFromHome(x)) ::: All employees in other countries work remotely from home.
¬∃x (Manager(x) ∧ RemoteFromHome(x)) ::: No managers work remotely from home.
(Manager(james) ∧ AppearToday(james)) ∨ (¬Manager(james) ∧ ¬AppearToday(james)) ::: James is either a manager and appears today, or neither.
